title: `@throws {never}` on an `async` foreign binding is refused: an async function does not throw at the call, it rejects afterwards
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, "Foreign Boundary": "Calling an unannotated foreign runtime value MUST add the checked `panic` case, because JavaScript and TypeScript may throw, reject, or violate a declaration." The word that decides this case is REJECT. The marker is an opt-out for the CALL, and an `async` function that fails returns normally and rejects later, so `@throws {never}` describes a channel it cannot cover. It is refused rather than silently ignored (poc/src/language/README.md, `SMITHERS1502`: 'so an author can tell a believed claim from a dropped one'). The untrusted spelling of the same binding already charges Panic — 09-foreign-calls/foreign-rejection-becomes-panic — which is precisely what made the TRUSTED direction the fail-open one: adding a marker to a binding removed a channel the unmarked binding had.
